proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t=m/n\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\) gives \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\).  Choose \(c_0<1\).  On the regime \(b_{nm}\le c_0\), the truncation in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) is inactive, and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_{nm}
 &=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}
   \sqrt{\log(en)}\sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\\
 &=K r^{3/2}\mu\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}
   \frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with
\[
 s_{nm}:=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q},
\]
there are positive constants \(C_-\) and \(C_+\), depending only on \(r,K,\mu,c_-,c_+\), such that
\[
 C_-s_{nm}\le b_{nm}\le C_+s_{nm}.
 \tag{1}
\]

We construct a constant-propensity subexperiment.  Since \(r\) is fixed, partition \(I\) into disjoint balanced blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\), and partition \(J\) into disjoint balanced blocks \(J_1,\ldots,J_r\); within each partition, block sizes differ by at most one.  Write \(N_s=|I_s|\) and \(M_s=|J_s|\).  For \(s\ge2\), let \(u_s=N_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_s}\), viewed in \(\mathbb R^n\), and, for every \(s\), let \(v_s=M_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{J_s}\), viewed in \(\mathbb R^m\).  Let \(u_0=N_1^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_1}\).  Fix \(k_0\in I_1\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K:=I_1\setminus\{k_0\}\), define
\[
 w_k=\frac{e_k-e_{k_0}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \delta=a\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}q},\qquad
 u_k=\frac{u_0+\delta w_k}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}},
 \tag{2}
\]
where the fixed constant \(a>0\) will be chosen below.  The vectors \(u_0\) and \(w_k\) are orthogonal unit vectors, so \(u_k\) is a unit vector.  Disjoint block supports give
\[
 U_k=(u_k,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\in\mathbb O_{n,r},
 \qquad V=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\in\mathbb O_{m,r}.
\]
Also set \(U_0=(u_0,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\), and define
\[
 M_k=\lambda_{nm}U_kV^\top\quad(k\in\mathcal K),
 \qquad M_0=\lambda_{nm}U_0V^\top.
 \tag{3}
\]

We verify every model restriction.  From (1)--(2),
\[
 \delta\sqrt n=a s_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}b_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}c_0.
 \tag{4}
\]
For a row in \(I_1\), the triangle inequality and (2) give
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top U_k\rVert_2
 \le N_1^{-1/2}+\delta/\sqrt2.
 \tag{5}
\]
For a row in \(I_s\), \(s\ge2\), its row norm is \(N_s^{-1/2}\).  Since \(r\) is fixed and the blocks are balanced,
\[
 \max_s\sqrt{n/N_s}\longrightarrow\sqrt r.
\]
The strict inequality \(\mu>1\) supplies positive slack between \(\sqrt r\) and \(\sqrt{\mu r}\).  First choose \(ac_0\) small enough, depending only on that slack and the fixed constants in (4), and then take \(n\) sufficiently large.  Equations (4)--(5) yield
\[
 \lVert U_k\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The same balanced-block calculation, without the perturbation, gives
\[
 \lVert V\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/m}
 \tag{7}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(m\).  Thus (6)--(7) verify the two incoherence assumptions.  By (3), all \(r\) nonzero singular values of \(M_k\) equal \(\lambda_{nm}\).  Consequently exact rank, the signal floor, and the condition-number bound hold, the last because \(1\le K\).

For all sufficiently large dimensions, balanced blocks satisfy \(N_s\ge n/(2r)\) and \(M_s\ge m/(2r)\).  Equations (2)--(3) imply
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|
 \le \frac{2r\lambda_{nm}}{\sqrt{nm}}
     +aB\sqrt{\frac{2r\log(en)}{qm}}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(c_1>0\) so that \(2rc_1\le1/4\).  Under \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\), the first term in (8) is at most \(B/4\).  The second is at most \(B/4\) for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), because \(q,r,a\) are fixed and aspect ratio is bounded.  Hence
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|\le B/2
 \tag{9}
\]
uniformly over \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\).

For each \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\), define a law \(P_k\) by setting \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\).  Independently over cells, draw \(Y_{ij}(1)\in\{-B,B\}\) with
\[
 P_k\{Y_{ij}(1)=B\}
 =h_{k,ij}:=\frac12\left(1+\frac{(M_k)_{ij}}B\right).
 \tag{10}
\]
Independently of all potential outcomes and independently over cells, draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), and record \(p_{ij}=q\).  Equation (9) puts every \(h_{k,ij}\) in \([1/4,3/4]\), while (10) gives \(E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)]=(M_k)_{ij}\).  Independence from all preceding cells in the row-major filtration gives
\[
 \mu^1_{ij}=E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=(M_k)_{ij},
 \qquad \mu^0_{ij}=0.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus the causal effect matrix \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\) is exactly \(M_k\), rather than being defined from the observed score.  Independence of \(A_{ij}\) from the potential outcomes after conditioning on the recorded past verifies sequential randomization.  The equality \(p_{ij}=q<1/2\) verifies overlap, and the support in (10), together with \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\), verifies bounded outcomes.  Equations (6)--(7), the singular-value calculation, and the aspect assumption verify all remaining member properties.  Hence
\[
 P_k\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}.
 \tag{12}
\]

We bound the information in \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\).  If \(x,y\in[-B/2,B/2]\), put \(s=(1+x/B)/2\) and \(t'=(1+y/B)/2\).  For fixed \(t'\in[1/4,3/4]\), the Bernoulli relative entropy
\(f(s)=s\log(s/t')+(1-s)\log((1-s)/(1-t'))\) satisfies
\[
 f(t')=f'(t')=0,
 \qquad f''(s)=\frac1{s(1-s)}\le\frac{16}3
 \quad\text{on }[1/4,3/4].
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\left(\frac{1+x/B}{2},\frac{1+y/B}{2}\right)
 \le \frac{2}{3}\frac{(x-y)^2}{B^2}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The assignment law and recorded propensity are identical under \(P_k\) and \(P_0\).  Conditional on \(A_{ij}=0\), the observed outcome is the common value zero; conditional on \(A_{ij}=1\), it has Bernoulli sign parameter \(h_{k,ij}\).  Independence over cells, (13), and direct factorization of the product likelihood yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 &=q\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{kl}(h_{k,ij},h_{0,ij})\\
 &\le \frac{Cq}{B^2}\lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{14}
\]
Only the first singular component differs in (3), and \(\lVert v_1\rVert_2=1\), so
\[
 \lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2
 =\lambda_{nm}^2\lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2.
\]
Orthogonality in (2) gives
\[
 \lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2
 =2\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}\right)
 \le\delta^2.
\]
Substitution of (2) into (14) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 \le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{15}
\]

The alternatives are separated in the required rowwise loss.  If \(k,\ell\in\mathcal K\) are distinct, inspect row \(k\).  On that row only the first columns of \(U_k\) and \(U_\ell\) can be nonzero, and (2) gives
\[
 \lVert e_k^\top U_k\rVert_2-\lVert e_k^\top U_\ell\rVert_2
 =\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
Right multiplication by any \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) preserves row norms.  The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}\lVert U_kR-U_\ell\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \ge\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathcal L(U_k,U_\ell)
 \ge \Delta_{nm}:=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
       \frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Equation (4) implies \(\delta\to0\), so eventually \(\delta\le1\).  Combining (1), (2), and (16), and using \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\), gives a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 \Delta_{nm}\ge c b_{nm}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, before the bounded denominator factor in (16), the exact ratio is
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\,\delta}{b_{nm}}
 =\frac{a}{K r^2\mu^{3/2}\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}}.
\]

It remains to derive the multiple-testing reduction.  Let \(D=|\mathcal K|=N_1-1\), let \(\Theta\) be uniform on \(\mathcal K\), and conditionally on \(\Theta=k\) draw the observed experiment from \(P_k^{\mathcal O}\).  With \(\overline P=D^{-1}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}P_k^{\mathcal O}\), expansion of the logarithms gives
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},\overline P)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
  -\operatorname{KL}(\overline P,P_0^{\mathcal O}).
\]
Nonnegativity of relative entropy and (15) imply
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)\le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{18}
\]
For any decoder \(\widehat\Theta\), let \(P_e=P(\widehat\Theta\ne\Theta)\).  Conditioning the entropy of \(\Theta\) first on the error indicator yields
\[
 H(\Theta\mid\mathcal O)\le\log2+P_e\log D.
\]
Since \(H(\Theta)=\log D\), this and (18) give
\[
 P_e\ge1-\frac{Ca^2\log(en)+\log2}{\log D}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Balanced blocks give \(D\asymp n\).  Choose \(a>0\) sufficiently small, depending only on the fixed quantities, so the right side of (19) is at least \(1/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Finally take any \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) and decode by a nearest member of \(\{U_k:k\in\mathcal K\}\) in the orthogonal-quotient \(2,\infty\) distance.  This quotient distance obeys the triangle inequality: compose two orthogonal alignments and use invariance of row norms under right orthogonal multiplication.  Thus, on a decoding error under \(P_k\), pairwise separation (16) and nearest-neighbor decoding imply
\[
 \mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)\ge\Delta_{nm}/2.
\]
Averaging over the uniform index, using (19), and then (17), gives
\[
 \sup_{k\in\mathcal K}E_{P_k}[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)]
 \ge\frac{\Delta_{nm}}4
 \ge c_2b_{nm}.
\]
By (12), this finite family is a subset of the frozen predictable class, and it has \(p_{ij}=q\) at every cell.  Taking the supremum over the full class and then the infimum over \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) proves the theorem.

Fix \(P\) in the predictable class and expose cells in the row-major order of \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}filtration}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\), each \(E_{ij}\) has conditional mean zero given \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  Sequential randomization and bounded outcomes give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}+
 \frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]\\
 &\le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The equality follows by conditioning once more on both potential outcomes and applying \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization}\); both divisions are valid by \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\).  Since \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\), conditional variance is no larger than this conditional second moment.  Moreover, bounded outcomes and overlap give \(|Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le B/q\), while conditional Jensen's inequality gives \(|M_{ij}|\le2B\).  Because \(q<1/2\),
\[
 |E_{ij}|\le \frac{2B}{q}.
\]

Introduce the self-adjoint dilation
\[
 \Delta_{ij}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 0&E_{ij}e_ie_j^\top\\
 E_{ij}e_je_i^\top&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its norm is \(|E_{ij}|\), and its square has diagonal blocks
\(E_{ij}^2e_ie_i^\top\) and \(E_{ij}^2e_je_j^\top\).  Therefore the predictable quadratic variation obeys
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_{i,j}E_P[\Delta_{ij}^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\right\rVert
 \le v_{nm}:=\frac{2B^2(n\vee m)}q.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\), applied to both signs of this \((n+m)\)-dimensional martingale, gives
\[
 P\{\lVert E\rVert\ge t\}
 \le2(n+m)\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2/2}{v_{nm}+R_{nm}t/3}\right\},
 \qquad R_{nm}=\frac{2B}{q}.
\]
The terminal dilation has operator norm \(\lVert E\rVert\).  With \(L_{nm}=\log(2(n+m))\), solving the quadratic inequality gives, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left\{\lVert E\rVert>
 \sqrt{2v_{nm}(L_{nm}+x)}+
 \frac{2R_{nm}}3(L_{nm}+x)\right\}\le e^{-x}.
\]
Integrating this tail is legitimate because every increment is bounded.  Using
\(\sqrt{L_{nm}+x}\le\sqrt{L_{nm}}+\sqrt x\),
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=1\), and
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\sqrt x\,dx<\infty\), we obtain
\[
 E_P\lVert E\rVert
 \le C B\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}
 =:C\eta_{nm}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Every bound is uniform in \(P\).

It remains to pass from operator error to the declared loss without imposing predictability on the singular factors.  Let \(P_U=UU^\top\), and let \((\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)\) be the leading rank-\(r\) singular triple of \(M+E\).  Exact rank gives \((I-P_U)M=0\).  The signal floor and the singular-value min--max formula imply, on \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\),
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat\Sigma)
 \ge\sigma_r(M)-\lVert E\rVert
 \ge\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert>0.
\]
Projecting \((M+E)\widehat V=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma\) onto the orthogonal complement of \(U\) gives
\[
 \lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert
 \le\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert}
 \le\frac{2\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
Diagonalizing the principal-angle cosines of \(U^\top\widehat U\) and using
\(2(1-\cos x)\le2\sin^2x\) supplies \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) such that
\[
 \lVert\widehat UR-U\rVert
 \le\sqrt2\lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert.
\]
Off the event \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\), the left side is at most two.  Since \(\lVert Q\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\lVert Q\rVert\), the two cases yield the deterministic inequality
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 \le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right).
 \tag{21}
\]
The fixed tie rule ensures that the leading left singular vectors of \(\mathcal P_r(M+E)\) are the chosen leading left singular vectors of \(M+E\).

The map \(x\mapsto1\wedge x\) is concave and nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\).  Jensen's inequality, (20), and \(1\wedge(Cx)\le C(1\wedge x)\) for \(C\ge1\) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 E_P\left[1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right]\\
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left[1\wedge\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{\sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}
 +\frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right]\\
 &=C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the declared class proves the proposition.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) gives the stronger uniform first-moment statement
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
The radius is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(q>0\), \(\lambda_{nm}>0\), and \(n,m\ge2\).  Markov's inequality therefore gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 P\!\left\{\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>
 t a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\right\}\le\frac Ct.
\]
This is the asserted uniform \(O_P(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) bound.  Neither the radius nor the moment proof uses a loading family, so no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\) occurs.

For the final assertion, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) supplies a sequence \(P_n\) in the same class and constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) such that \(b_{nn}\to0\) and
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_n\!\left\{
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>c_0\right\}\ge c_1.
\]
If the IPW--SVD loss were uniformly \(O_P(b_{nm})\), then for \(\varepsilon=c_1/2\) some fixed \(T<\infty\) would make the probability at threshold \(Tb_{nn}\) at most \(\varepsilon\) eventually.  Since \(Tb_{nn}<c_0\) eventually, this contradicts the preceding display.  The witness evaluates only \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\), and therefore proves no impossibility result for a different estimator.

added_lemmas.statement:
The matrix \(Q^{\mathrm D}\) has orthonormal columns and, viewed as a constant estimator, belongs to \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  Whenever the target obeys \(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\), its normalized maximum-row loss satisfies the pathwise inequality
\[
 \mathcal L(Q^{\mathrm D},U)\le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\vartheta=\pi/(n+1)\).  For integers \(s,t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the product-to-sum identity and the finite geometric-series identity give
\[
 2\sum_{i=1}^n\sin(is\vartheta)\sin(it\vartheta)
 =\sum_{i=1}^n\{\cos(i(s-t)\vartheta)-\cos(i(s+t)\vartheta)\}
 =(n+1)\mathbf 1\{s=t\}.
\]
For clarity, the last equality follows by taking real parts in
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n e^{ih i\vartheta}
 =\frac{e^{ih\vartheta}-e^{ih(n+1)\vartheta}}
        {1-e^{ih\vartheta}}
\]
for each nonzero integer \(h\) appearing above; the case \(s=t\) then uses
\(\sin^2 x=(1-\cos(2x))/2\).  Every denominator is nonzero because
\(0<|h|<2(n+1)\) in the nonzero cases.  Since \(r\le n\), the displayed orthogonality identity applies to all columns selected in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}hybrid\mbox{-}estimator}\), and hence
\[
 (Q^{\mathrm D})^\top Q^{\mathrm D}=I_r.
\]
Thus \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\).  It is deterministic, so it is measurable with respect to the observed sigma-field \(\mathcal O_{n,m}\); the definition of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) in \(\mathrm{def:observed\mbox{-}estimators}\) gives \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).

For every row \(i\), \(|\sin(is\vartheta)|\le1\), so
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_2^2
 =\frac2{n+1}\sum_{s=1}^r\sin^2(is\vartheta)
 \le\frac{2r}{n+1}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \lVert Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}.
\]
The minimum over \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:rowwise\mbox{-}loss}\) is no larger than its value at \(R=I_r\).  The rowwise triangle inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence}\) therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L(Q^{\mathrm D},U)
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\lVert Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_{2,\infty}
       +\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\right)\\
 &\le\sqrt{\frac{2n}{\mu(n+1)}}+1
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is deterministic and hence holds on every sample path.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every \(n,m\ge2\), the hybrid estimator satisfies \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)\right]
 \le C\bigl(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\bigr).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The quantity \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) is deterministic and strictly positive because \(n,m\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), \(\mu\ge1\), \(B>0\), \(q>0\), and \(\lambda_{nm}>0\).  The recorded score is a measurable function of \((A,Y,p)\), and rank projection followed by the fixed tie rule is measurable; hence \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) by \(\mathrm{def:observed\mbox{-}estimators}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:deterministic\mbox{-}sine\mbox{-}fallback}\) gives \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  Selection between these two estimators by the deterministic event \(\{a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\}\) preserves observed-data measurability and orthonormality, proving \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).

If \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\), the hybrid definition gives \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}=\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\), and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) yields
\[
 \sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)
 \le C_1a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}
 =C_1(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}).
\]
If \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1\), the hybrid definition and the pathwise sine-frame inequality give
\[
 \sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)
 \le1+\sqrt{2/\mu}
 \le1+\sqrt2
 =(1+\sqrt2)(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}),
\]
where \(\mu\ge1\) was used in the second inequality.  Taking
\(C=\max\{C_1,1+\sqrt2\}\) proves the uniform assertion in both cases.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(r\), \(K\), and \(\mu>1\).  There are constants \(c_0,c_1,c,C>0\), depending only on these fixed quantities, \(q\), and the aspect bounds, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), whenever \(b_{nm}\le c_0\) and \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\),
\[
 c b_{nm}\le
 \inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]
 \le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}).
\]
The recorded estimator separately satisfies
\(\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  Its endogenous-target obstruction is estimator-specific and does not imply that every member of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) has risk bounded away from zero.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The first inequality is Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:adaptive\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}lower}\), whose constant-propensity alternatives lie in the same predictable class and whose risk is the same expected normalized maximum-row loss.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:hybrid\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) proves both that \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) and the last inequality.  Evaluating the infimum over \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) at this one admissible data-driven estimator proves the middle inequality.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) gives the separate recorded-IPW bound.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) evaluates only \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\); it therefore cannot be converted into a lower bound for all \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  These observations prove the displayed bracket and the stated scope.

added_lemmas.statement:
For arbitrary real \(n\times m\) matrices \(A_1,A_0\),
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_1-A_0)
 \le\operatorname{rank}(A_1)+\operatorname{rank}(A_0).
\]
The converse implication from low rank of the difference to low rank of both arms fails even under the entrywise envelope \(B\): there are matrices \(A_0,A_1\) with entries bounded in absolute value by \(B\), both of rank \(n\wedge m\), whose difference has rank one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
 (A_1-A_0)x=A_1x-A_0x
 \in\operatorname{im}(A_1)+\operatorname{im}(A_0).
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{im}(A_1-A_0)\subseteq
\operatorname{im}(A_1)+\operatorname{im}(A_0)\).  Taking dimensions and using
\(\dim(S+T)\le\dim S+\dim T\) for finite-dimensional subspaces proves the rank inequality.

For the witness put \(s=n\wedge m\), let \((e_t)_{t=1}^n\) and \((f_t)_{t=1}^m\) be the standard bases, and define
\[
 C=\frac B2\sum_{t=1}^s e_tf_t^\top,
 \qquad A_0=C,
 \qquad A_1=C+\frac B4e_1f_1^\top.
\]
Every entry of \(A_0\) has absolute value at most \(B/2\), and every entry of \(A_1\) has absolute value at most \(3B/4\), so the declared envelope holds.  The leading \(s\times s\) diagonal block of \(A_0\) has diagonal entries \(B/2\), while that of \(A_1\) has first diagonal entry \(3B/4\) and all remaining diagonal entries \(B/2\).  Because \(B>0\), both blocks are nonsingular and both rectangular matrices have the maximal rank \(s\).  Finally,
\(A_1-A_0=(B/4)e_1f_1^\top\) has rank one.  This proves the claimed failure of the converse without making any class-containment or rate assertion.

proposed.name: Deterministic-sine and recorded-IPW hybrid estimator
proposed.construction:
Define the deterministic sine frame \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) by
\[
 Q^{\mathrm D}_{is}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n+1}}
 \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi i s}{n+1}\right),
 \qquad i\in I,\quad s\in\{1,\ldots,r\}.
\]
Define
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left[1\wedge\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{\sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}
 +\frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
The observed-data hybrid estimator is
\[
 \widehat U^{\mathrm H}=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat U^{\mathrm I},&a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1,\\
 Q^{\mathrm D},&a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The branch is deterministic because it depends only on the declared dimensions and class parameters.
inputs: The dimensions and declared class parameters, together with the recorded IPW--SVD fit.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD upper bound under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means. Only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) is shared: their rowwise matrix-error theorem has its own \(\log^4\) factor, whereas \(b_{nm}\) also has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) conversion to normalized effect-subspace loss.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether the minimax expected normalized maximum-row risk is of order \(b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\), of constant order, or at an intermediate rate; only after that decide the sharp normalized constant and least-favorable propensity structure.
open_obligations.obstruction: The constant-propensity packing lower-bounds every estimator only at order \(b_{nm}\). The sine hybrid supplies a constant upper endpoint, while the endogenous-target construction obstructs only recorded IPW--SVD. None of these results gives an estimator-independent lower bound above \(b_{nm}\) or a uniformly vanishing observed-data estimator on the full predictable class.
open_obligations.attempted: A row-local constant-propensity Fano packing, the matrix-Freedman IPW upper, the accepted endogenous-target witness, and a deterministic sine-frame fallback were combined. They close the bracket from \(c b_{nm}\) to a constant but do not identify the intervening minimax order.
open_obligations.partial_result: The constant-propensity packing proves a positive \(b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\)-normalized lower bound when \(\mu>1\).  The sine-frame hybrid is one observed-data estimator with risk at most \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{n_\ell m_\ell})\).  Nonemptiness under bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{n_\ell m_\ell}\le2B\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio, the resulting \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}\) and blind \(d\) radii are bounded below by order \(\sqrt{\log n_\ell}\), so this uniform upper endpoint is eventually only constant.  The endogenous-factor witness proves that recorded IPW--SVD need not attain the \(b\) scale, but it gives no lower bound for every observed-data estimator.  Hence the presently proved minimax bracket runs from \(c b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\) to a constant and does not determine \(C_\star\).

prose_updates.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the IPW entry errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array. Writing \(R^\star_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\), the common expected-loss result is now \(c b_{nm}\le R^\star_{nm}\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\). The explicit observed-data hybrid uses recorded IPW--SVD only when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and otherwise reports a deterministic sine frame. Recorded IPW--SVD separately retains its \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) guarantee and estimator-specific obstruction. Nonemptiness under bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this implies \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\). Thus the honest unresolved minimax gap is from \(b_{nm}\) to a constant, and the uniform blind-resolution radius is nonshrinking in this regime. The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a blind-scaling failure witness and HeartSteps II stress design; simultaneous dense-query radii retain a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not determine effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment. A constant-propensity causal packing gives the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\). Matrix Freedman gives the larger recorded-IPW radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), while the deterministic-frame hybrid gives a uniform \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) upper bound. On every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect class the loose radius is eventually at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so the remaining minimax problem is a \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant gap, not a matched-rate theorem.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with a concrete observed-data hybrid, a separate IPW-specific obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost remains separate from all subspace scales.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the constant-propensity minimax lower benchmark, the expected recorded-IPW spectral bound, the pathwise sine-frame bound, and the hybrid expected-risk upper in one normalized maximum-row criterion. It records the unresolved estimator-independent rate gap, shows that nonempty fixed-complexity classes make both the spectral and blind radii nonshrinking, retains the explicit Markov witness, and supplies direct finite-sample simultaneous bands with their own family-size inflation.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and no estimated treatment nuisance; its expected-risk guarantee follows from matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace inequality. The hybrid switches deterministically, using that fit when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and the first \(r\) columns of the discrete-sine frame otherwise. On nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect classes, \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), so the hybrid eventually uses the constant-risk fallback. The blind procedure estimates a clipped row fraction and is controlled only at \(d_{nm}\); because \(d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\) in the same regime, its uniform resolution does not shrink. Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes, not feasible multiplier exactness.

prose_updates.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment. The only shared feature used here is the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\). Their public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 carry their own \(\log^4\) factor, impose armwise assumptions, and bound matrix-row error. In contrast, \(b_{nm}\) also contains \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the factor \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) converting matrix perturbation to normalized effect-subspace loss. No matched-rate transfer is claimed. Algebraically, arm matrices \(A_1,A_0\) always satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A_1-A_0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A_1)+\operatorname{rank}(A_0)\). The converse fails even for bounded matrices: with \(s=n\wedge m\), \(C=(B/2)\sum_{t=1}^s e_tf_t^\top\), \(A_0=C\), and \(A_1=C+(B/4)e_1f_1^\top\), both arms have rank \(s\) and entries bounded by \(B\), while their difference has rank one. This is only an algebraic separation; it asserts neither full-class containment nor a rate transfer.

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen give two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise; they inform the perturbation and packing architecture but not the predictable causal class. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi and Sun, Zhu, and Dubin give upper-error results for their own arm or completion models, and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan study Frobenius risk under fixed heterogeneous sampling. Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean estimation under exogenous factors. These results do not close the present estimator-independent subspace gap.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the predictable IPW martingale reduction, and Tropp supplies the matrix Freedman inequality. Khan and Ugander analyze a different scalar normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are not claims about that method. The direct simultaneous theorem keeps \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) outside \(b_{nm}\). Saved propensities and the Markov omission stress test are operationally relevant to the HeartSteps II consumer described by Spruijt-Metz et al.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target is \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(\mu^1-\mu^0)\), identified by the conditional mean of the recorded IPW score. Writing \(R^\star_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\), the proved headline is \(c b_{nm}\le R^\star_{nm}\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\). The separate recorded-IPW guarantee is \(\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), and its counterexample is estimator-specific. In a nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, the hybrid endpoint is constant because \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), whereas \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\); determining the true order between them is the live question. Blind-fit loss and the observed blind-versus-recorded diagnostic resolve total drift only up to the nonshrinking radius \(d_{nm}\). The Markov witness is a HeartSteps II stress design, and simultaneous dense-query bands have a separate entropy multiplier.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The matrix-Freedman route controls operator norm and then pays \(\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\) in the deterministic subspace conversion. Bounded outcomes imply \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\) whenever the class is nonempty, so at fixed complexity this recorded-IPW radius cannot shrink and is at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\). The sine-frame hybrid repairs the uniform upper endpoint only to a constant and eventually ignores the data in that regime. The frozen class permits target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes; the accepted construction makes this substantive for IPW--SVD but does not rule out a different estimator with vanishing risk. The blind radius \(d_{nm}\) is likewise at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so its uniform diagnostic resolution is nonshrinking. No residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean. The proved statistical result is a lower/reference benchmark \(c b_{nm}\) and a constant-risk observed-data hybrid upper \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) in the same expected normalized maximum-row loss. These endpoints are not claimed to match. Recorded IPW--SVD retains its separate \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) bound, and the adaptive endogenous-target witness refutes \(b_{nm}\)-attainment only for that estimator. On nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect classes, the spectral and blind radii are nonshrinking; no unconditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale blind criterion is claimed. The \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for the newly defined blind procedure and a HeartSteps II stress design, not a refutation of a published normalization method. Simultaneous inference is supplied by conservative direct-IPW radii with a separate query-family factor.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large pair \((n,m)\) and choose
\(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\), which is possible by the stated nonemptiness condition.  The bounded-outcome assumption gives
\(-B\le Y_{ij}(a)\le B\) almost surely for every \(i\in I\), \(j\in J\), and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Order preservation of conditional expectation therefore gives, almost surely,
\[
 -B\le \mu^a_{ij}
 =E_P[Y_{ij}(a)\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\le B.
\]
By the definition \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\), it follows that \(|M_{ij}|\le2B\) for every cell.  Hence
\[
 \lVert M\rVert_F^2=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^m M_{ij}^2
 \le4B^2nm.
\]
The squared Frobenius norm is the sum of the squared singular values, so nonnegativity of those summands implies \(\sigma_r(M)\le\lVert M\rVert_F\).  The signal-floor assumption and the last display thus give
\[
 \lambda_{nm}\le\sigma_r(M)\le\lVert M\rVert_F
 \le2B\sqrt{nm}.
\]
Although the intermediate matrices can be random under a predictable law, both the bounded-outcome and signal-floor inequalities hold almost surely; since their endpoints are deterministic, the displayed inequality is a necessary condition for class nonemptiness.

Put \(s_n=\sqrt{\log(en)/n}\), so \(s_n\to0\).  Write \(t_b\) for the untruncated expression in the definition of \(b_{nm}\).  The preceding signal bound, positivity of \(B\) and \(\lambda_{nm}\), and the elementary inequality
\(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\ge n^{-1/2}\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 t_b
 &=\frac{B\sqrt{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\log(en)}
 K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}
 \sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\\
 &\ge \frac{K r^{3/2}\mu}{2\sqrt q}\,s_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(c_b=K r^{3/2}\mu/(2\sqrt q)>0\).  Since \(c_bs_n\le1\) eventually and \(b_{nm}=1\wedge t_b\), monotonicity of \(x\mapsto1\wedge x\) gives
\[
 b_{nm}\ge c_b s_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Next write \(t_a\) for the entire untruncated expression inside the square brackets defining \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  Because
\[
 \frac{n\vee m}{nm}=\frac1{n\wedge m}\ge\frac1n,
 \qquad
 \log(e(n+m))\ge\log(en),
\]
the signal bound gives
\[
 t_a\ge
 \frac1{2\sqrt{nm}}
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}
 \ge\frac1{2\sqrt q}\,s_n.
\]
The right-hand side is at most one eventually.  Therefore
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}
 =\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}(1\wedge t_a)
 \ge\frac1{2\sqrt{q\mu r}}\sqrt{\log(en)}.
\]
Likewise, if \(t_d\) denotes the entire untruncated expression inside the square brackets defining \(d_{nm}\), retaining only its nonnegative square-root term gives
\[
 t_d\ge
 \frac1{2q\sqrt{nm}}
 \sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 \ge\frac1{2q}s_n,
\]
and hence
\[
 d_{nm}\ge\frac1{2q\sqrt{\mu r}}\sqrt{\log(en)}.
\]
This proves the three asserted scale floors, with, for example,
\(c_a=(2\sqrt{q\mu r})^{-1}\) and
\(c_d=(2q\sqrt{\mu r})^{-1}\).  Since \(\log(en)\to\infty\), the last two lower bounds also prove that neither radius shrinks.

It remains to verify the conditional comparison when \(b_{nm}=o(1)\).  The bounded aspect-ratio assumption gives
\[
 n\vee m\asymp n,
 \qquad
 \log(e(n+m))\asymp\log(en),
 \qquad
 \sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\asymp\sqrt n.
\]
Because \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed positive constants, these relations and the geometric-rate definition imply
\[
 t_b\asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
Since \(b_{nm}=1\wedge t_b=o(1)\), one has \(b_{nm}<1\) eventually, and consequently \(t_b=b_{nm}\to0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\log(en)}{\sqrt{n\log(en)}}
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Using fixed \(q\), the aspect relations, and this limit in the definitions of \(t_a\) and \(t_d\) yields
\[
 t_a\asymp t_d\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}asymp t_b=o(1).
\]
Thus the truncations defining \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are also eventually inactive.  Substitution gives
\[
 b_{nm}\asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}},
 \qquad
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\asymp d_{nm}\asymp
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
